title: Audit your agent's session logs before an account appeal
summary: A developer whose Claude account was banned mid-task had Codex audit 7,478 local session records for an appeal; they report no safety flags found, but the appeal was denied.
agent_role: Claude Code made the code changes, testing and production rollout for a model upgrade. Codex then screened the session history and transcripts for anything that might have triggered a ban; the human wrote and sent the appeal.
outcome: Author reports Codex found zero safety refusals or warnings in 7,478 records, but Anthropic denied the appeal and changed the cited reason.
what_they_did: The poster had Claude Code switch their app to Google's new Gemini model and roll it out to production. On another machine their Claude account was banned mid-task. They asked Codex to audit 76 sessions and 52 transcript files from their Mac to see if any prompt or tool call broke a rule, then used the findings in a full-disclosure appeal.
how_it_went: They say Codex found zero safety refusals or warnings across 7,478 timestamped records. The appeal was still denied, with the reason switched to a general usage policy. Codex finished the integration work instead.
worth_knowing: They audited only the Mac and overlooked the other machine where the production rollout ran. They also suspect their overly candid appeal may have given reviewers a different rule to cite.
prompt: Review my local coding-agent session logs in [log folder path] from [start date] to [end date]. List every session and transcript file you checked, with counts. Flag any prompt, tool call or output that could look like a policy violation, a safety refusal or unusual automated activity. For each flag, quote the record and explain why. Then write a short, factual summary I could use in an account appeal. Show me the summary for review; do not send anything.

curation.rationale: A real multi-step use: Claude Code shipped a model upgrade to production, then Codex audited 7,478 local log records to build an account-ban appeal. The audit idea is unusual, but it is one person's account and the post is mostly a ban story.
